    How this estimate works

    Weekly hours = tasks × minutes × working days ÷ 60. Monthly hours use 4.33 weeks. Workload cost = monthly hours × hourly staff cost. Returned capacity = monthly hours × your estimated workload reduction. Its value uses the same hourly rate. Net monthly value subtracts recurring costs; payback divides setup cost by positive net monthly value.

    These are planning estimates, not guaranteed savings or a quote. Capacity value is not necessarily cash saved or fewer employees. Validate the assumptions against a real workflow and include review time, all operating costs, and implementation effort.

    A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

    Let’s clear
    things up.

    Can you work with our existing tools?

    Usually, yes. We assess your current apps, available integrations, and API access first. The aim is to connect what already works for you and identify any gaps before agreeing the scope.

    Will automation replace my team?

    The first goal is to remove repetitive workload. Your people still handle relationships, judgement, and exceptions. Depending on the process, automation can help you manage more activity without hiring additional staff for routine tasks.

    How much does an automation cost?

    Pricing depends on the workflow, integration complexity, and support you need. We agree scope and costs before work starts. See how projects are quoted.

    How do you handle sensitive business data?

    We agree which data a workflow needs, who can access it, and which tools will process it. Read our approach to data, approvals, and handover.

    What happens on the demo call?

    We discuss your current process, walk through a relevant automation example, and identify a practical starting point. Share the tools you use and the tasks taking up your team’s time so we can make the conversation useful.
